summary: PHP support is a registry addition following the Java/Swift OO pattern. The grammar (tree-sitter-php v0.25.2, tagged 2026-11-19) uses unnamed base_clause and class_interface_clause children, not fields, so the inheritance walk must differ from java.rs. Recommend a full-scope handler (approach A) that matches the issue scope. Note the maintainers' process note: external PRs are not accepted; this report is for internal planning only.

conventions.commits: Conventional Commits with GPG signing and DCO sign-off (git commit -S --signoff); example: 'feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)' (dbc2971). Every commit body carries 'Signed-off-by: Hugues Clouatre'.
conventions.testing: Unit tests live in #[cfg(test)] mod tests at the bottom of each languages/<lang>.rs (parse helper, then query/handler assertions, test_<lang>_* or queries_compile naming). Registry tests are in languages/mod.rs and lang.rs. Integration tests live in crates/aptu-coder/tests/*.rs and use tests/common call_tool_raw plus tempfile::NamedTempFile::with_suffix_in(ext, cwd). Run with cargo test.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy -- -D warnings (CI uses cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings); cargo deny check advisories licenses bans. Workspace lints deny unwrap_used, expect_used (test code exempt via cfg_attr) and undocumented_unsafe_blocks; unreachable_pub is warn; new Cargo.lock entries must be 7 days old or the check fails.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option or empty Vec; text extraction is bounds-checked via get_node_text or an end_byte <= source.len() guard; registry lookups return None for unknown languages; query compile failures map to ParserError::QueryError with the language name. No unwrap or expect outside tests.

patterns: Registry pattern: each language is a file in languages/ exporting *_QUERY consts and optional handlers, then a match arm in get_language_info (languages/mod.rs) and a match arm in get_ts_language, plus a pub mod line and an EXTENSION_MAP row in lang.rs.

Required capture names consumed by parser_elements.rs: element uses @function, @class, @func_name, @method_name, @class_name, @type_name; call uses @call; import uses @import_path; type refs use @type_ref; defuse uses prefixes write., read., writeread.
DEFUSE prefix classification in parser_elements.rs (write./read./writeread.) and read-site dedupe by start byte: write captures must target the same node as read captures to dedupe correctly.

Inheritance handler signature fn(&Node, &str) -> Vec<String> with 'extends X' / 'implements X' (java.rs) or 'extends' / 'conforms' (swift.rs) prefixes; parser_elements.rs calls the handler on any captured class node, so handlers must tolerate interface, trait and enum nodes.
Import fallback: unknown import node kinds store trimmed full text as the module (parser_elements.rs fallback arm), so a single namespace_use_declaration query works without a new match arm.

Tree-sitter grammar crate version aligns with the workspace tree-sitter 0.27 API via tree-sitter-language 0.1.x (already in Cargo.lock at 0.1.9); tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 depends on tree-sitter-language ^0.1, so no core API mismatch is expected.

constraints: Issue #1864 says external pull requests are not accepted; the maintainers implement it in-house. The output is planning input only.

Scope in #1864: php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance; registry wiring in languages/mod.rs and lang.rs; unit tests in php.rs; one integration test file under crates/aptu-coder/tests/; README update. Not in scope: extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type, trait use resolution, property and constant extraction, attributes, namespace aliasing, .phtml/.inc/.module/.php5 extensions, tool or schema changes.
Use LANGUAGE_PHP (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY): LANGUAGE_PHP accepts inline HTML and <?php tags; the PHP-only grammar does not, which would break the HTML-template acceptance criterion.

Every new Cargo.lock entry must be at least 7 days old. tree-sitter-php v0.25.2 was tagged 2026-11-19T16:21:30Z (commit date), about 8.3 days before this run. The crates.io publish date was not verifiable offline, so re-check it before adding the dependency.

The issue requires cargo deny check advisories licenses bans to pass without SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK. deny.toml's [licenses] allow list includes MIT (line 20), which covers tree-sitter-php's MIT license; the advisories and bans gates were not run, since cargo deny needs network access.
Workspace lints deny unwrap_used and expect_used outside test code, and tests may use them through cfg_attr exemptions.
README 'Supported Languages' omits Swift (added in #1742), and lib.rs's doc comment also omits it; a PHP PR that edits the list should decide whether to fix Swift in the same change.

test_coverage: Every language module has an inline test module. java.rs has test_java_element_query_happy_path, test_java_extract_inheritance and test_defuse_query_write_site. swift.rs has queries_compile, set_language_smoke, element_query_matches_class_and_function and two extract_inheritance tests (superclass plus protocols, no inheritance). css.rs has rule-set, import and empty-file tests. languages/mod.rs has get_language_info_known/unknown, get_ts_language_known/unknown and a table test covering tsx, fortran, markdown, css and yaml. lang.rs has language_for_extension happy and edge tests plus an ECMAScript pattern test that automatically covers every EXTENSION_MAP row. aptu-coder/tests/integration_tests.rs has analyze_file tests, including test_analyze_file_unsupported_extension, but no per-language integration test for Java, Swift or CSS was found, so the PHP integration test sets a new pattern. Gap: no existing test asserts a call-query or import-query output per language inside the language modules.

approaches.name: A: Full-scope handler matching the issue (recommended)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (six declaration kinds), CALL_QUERY (free, member, nullsafe, static calls), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type and name type refs), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (variable_name writes and reads), and extract_inheritance that walks the base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Wire 'php' in lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP and supported_languages), mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info, get_ts_language, registry test row), add tree-sitter-php to the root and core Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, update README, add unit tests in php.rs and one integration test file.
pros: Follows the Java and Swift OO pattern exactly
DEFUSE_QUERY keeps def-use results populated for .php files
Inheritance is correct for the grammar's real node layout
cons: Largest diff: about 7 files plus a new test file
Needs a grammar-node check for each query (done here against node-types.json), so higher verification cost
Lockfile age gate: the grammar tag is about 8 days old, so timing matters

approaches.name: B: Minimal element, call and import only
approaches.description: Ship php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY, set REFERENCE_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance to None, and wire the registry without the inheritance walk. Keep the Cargo and README changes.
pros: Smallest verification surface; fewest node kinds to confirm
Fastest path past the 7-day age gate and cargo deny
cons: Violates the issue's five-constant scope and the acceptance criterion for extends and implements
Def-use returns no sites for .php (parser.rs returns empty when defuse is None), which is a visible gap
Requires a second PR to finish inheritance

approaches.name: C: Derive the queries from the upstream tags.scm
approaches.description: Use tree-sitter-php's queries/tags.scm (name: (name) captures on function_definition, method_declaration, class, interface, trait, namespace and function/member/scoped call sites) as the source of ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY, and rename its @definition.* and @reference.* captures to the names parser_elements.rs consumes (@function, @class, @class_name, @func_name, @call). Still add DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance by hand.
pros: Reuses queries that upstream maintains and tests against the same grammar version
Lower risk of drifting from grammar node kinds
cons: tags.scm is not packaged in the crate's Rust API; TAGS_QUERY would need to be copied into the repo, which adds a licensed vendored file
Capture names differ from what the parser expects; renaming is a manual step
tags.scm does not cover enum_declaration, so ELEMENT_QUERY still needs a hand-written pattern

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets the issue's acceptance criteria. Its key risk is the inheritance walk: java.rs's child_by_field_name("superclass") pattern would silently return nothing for PHP, because the grammar has no such field and uses base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Verify the crate version and its publish age, and check the cargo deny output, before editing Cargo.lock.

element_query_draft:
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration

(trait_declaration

(enum_declaration

Node kinds and field: function_definition.name (name), method_declaration.name (name), class_declaration.name (name), interface_declaration.name (name), trait_declaration.name (name), enum_declaration.name (name). Source: php/src/node-types.json fields. Covers every declaration kind the grammar defines with a body that the issue asks for: function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration. anonymous_function and arrow_function are closures, not declarations, and are excluded.
defuse_query_draft:
(assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @write.assign))
(augmented_assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @writeread.augmented))
(update_expression argument: (variable_name (name) @writeread.update))
(simple_parameter name: (variable_name (name) @write.param))
(static_variable_declaration name: (variable_name (name) @write.static))
(global_declaration (variable_name (name) @write.global))
(variable_name (name) @read.usage)

Basis: java.rs DEFUSE_QUERY, which is:
(local_variable_declaration declarator: (variable_declarator name: (identifier) @write.local))
(assignment_expression left: (identifier) @write.assign)
(update_expression (identifier) @writeread.update)
(identifier) @read.usage

PHP local variables are variable_name nodes whose child is name (node-types: variable_name children [name]); the write and read patterns therefore capture the inner name node, so the symbol text is the name without the $ sigil. Assignment left (assignment_expression.left includes variable_name), augmented_assignment_expression.left, update_expression.argument, simple_parameter.name (variable_name), static_variable_declaration.name (variable_name) and global_declaration children (variable_name) were confirmed in node-types.json. Put write patterns before the read pattern so that the byte-offset dedupe in parser_elements.rs keeps the write kind.
inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source inspected: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php master (tag v0.25.2). php/src/grammar.json and php/src/node-types.json were fetched with gh api and read directly (class_declaration, base_clause and class_interface_clause rules, plus field lists). The rule shape written as keyword('class') etc. is the common/define-grammar.js form, quoted through Context7 from the same repo; it matches grammar.json. class_declaration has exactly three fields in node-types.json: name (type name, required), body (declaration_list, required), attributes (attribute_list, optional). There is no superclass, base_classes, parent_class or interfaces field; child_by_field_name("superclass") as used in java.rs would return None. The grammar rule is: optional(field('attributes', attribute_list)), repeat(_modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', name), optional(base_clause), optional(class_interface_clause), field('body', declaration_list). Walk to extends: iterate the unnamed children of the class_declaration node (node.child(i) or a TreeCursor), select the child whose kind() == "base_clause"; its rule is SEQ(keyword 'extends', commaSep1(_name)) and node-types lists its children as name, qualified_name, relative_name. For each named child of base_clause (named_child(j)) whose kind is name, qualified_name or relative_name, emit format!("extends {text}"). Walk to implements: iterate the same unnamed children, select kind() == "class_interface_clause"; its rule is SEQ(keyword 'implements', commaSep1(_name)) with the same child kinds; for each named child emit format!("implements {text}"). The keyword tokens 'extends' and 'implements' are ALIAS nodes with named:false, so they never appear in named_child iteration and must not be matched. Order is the grammar sequence: base_clause (if present) is always before class_interface_clause, so output order is extends entries first, then implements entries. Interface: interface_declaration also uses optional(base_clause), so 'interface I extends A, B' yields extends entries; trait_declaration has no clause; enum_declaration uses optional(class_interface_clause) and no base_clause. Test oracle from the upstream corpus (test/corpus/declarations.txt): class A extends B parses to (class_declaration name: (name) (base_clause (name)) body: (declaration_list)).
